page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware allocation consists of 32 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The processor incorporates a 260 MB Level 3 cache along with instruction extensions including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) for matrix and vector computations.

Memory capacity is configured at 1024.0 GB, establishing a high ratio of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local persistence is supplied via 7560 GB of NVMe SSD storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No discrete GPUs are provisioned in this configuration.

Benchmark results show high memory subsystem throughput, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching 238.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieving 137.13 GB/sec, both placing in the upper 25 percent. In compute testing, Geekbench scores reached 2086.0 for single-core and 16779.0 for multi-core. In application-oriented tests, the machine delivered 43.41 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 44.43 GB/sec.

The 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio provides substantial cost efficiency for enterprise software licensed on a per-core basis that simultaneously requires massive memory pools. The primary architectural tradeoff is the lower core count relative to the terabyte-scale RAM allocation, which limits raw parallel compute scaling. Best-fit workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, and memory-bound data analytics pipelines with high local scratch storage demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration extensions. Designed for memory-intensive architectures, it supplies 1024.0 GB of RAM alongside 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate strong memory throughput, registering 238.84 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 137.13 GB/sec in write bandwidth, as well as an upper-quartile Geekbench multi-core score of 16779.0. In synthetic service benchmarks, the instance yielded 43.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 44.43 GB/sec in static web throughput. By pairing a high 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with dedicated local NVMe capacity, the instance minimizes core-based licensing costs for enterprise in-memory databases, large cache layers, and analytical data workloads.
